item.title: Supreme Court Allows Trump to Pursue Mail Voting Limits, for Now
item.description: The administration asked the court to clear the way for President Trump’s order that creates “state citizenship lists” and directs the Postal Service to decide who gets a mail-in ballot.
item.dc:creator: Abbie VanSickle and Ann E. Marimow
item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times
item.media:description: Volunteers processing mail-in ballots on Nov. 5, 2024, in Dearborn, Mich.

item.title: Trump Has Quietly Sought Control Over Postal Service to Transform U.S. Elections
item.description: That effort got new attention on Monday, when the Supreme Court allowed preparations for mail voting curbs to proceed. The justices said it is not a final determination on the order’s legality.
item.dc:creator: Zolan Kanno-Youngs, Adam Sella and Nick Corasaniti
item.media:description: President Trump and his allies are trying to transform the U.S. Postal Service into a key player in their efforts to transform the nation’s elections.

item.title: How U.S.-Canada Tariff Negotiations Turned Into an All-Out Trade War
item.description: Detailed accounts of the final hours of the negotiations show that, while the United States offered Canada what it said was the best deal of any country, what Canada had to give up in exchange was seen as unthinkable.
item.dc:creator: Matina Stevis-Gridneff and Ana Swanson
item.category: Office of the United States Trade Representative
item.media:description: Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada speaking about the trade dispute with the United States on Monday at the Davie Shipyard in Levis, Quebec.

item.title: U.S. Tariffs Could Price Canadian Firms Out of U.S. and Threaten Thousands of Jobs
item.description: The 50 percent tariffs President Trump imposed on Canadian exports to the United States will make it impossible for many Canadian companies to continue to sell to the U.S. market, economists say.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.media:description: Harvested logs in British Columbia in 2023. Canada’s forestry industry may be hit particularly hard by the latest American tariffs.

item.title: Trump Administration Aims to Revoke Visas of Foreign Citizens Applying for Asylum
item.description: The State Department, in a move that could affect as many as 200,000 visa holders and asylum applicants, has begun its review. Cancellations could occur in waves.
item.dc:creator: Edward Wong
item.media:description: “Obtaining a visa in order to seek asylum is fraud — which is grounds for visa revocation,” Tommy Pigott, a State Department spokesman, said in a statement.

item.title: Trump Officials Propose Charging More Than $100,000 for Skilled Worker Visas
item.description: The proposal comes after the Trump administration ran into legal challenges in its attempt to attach a similar fee to the H-1B visa last year.
item.dc:creator: Madeleine Ngo
item.media:description: The Trump administration has called for an overhaul of the H-1B visa program, saying it has unfairly allowed companies to sideline Americans and hire foreign workers at lower pay.

item.title: Trump’s Attempt to Strangle Iran’s Economy Depends on China’s Cooperation
item.description: The U.S. has spent 20 years promising ‘crippling sanctions’ on Iran. But the latest effort comes with a reverse twist, after military action failed to accomplish President Trump’s goals.
item.dc:creator: David E. Sanger
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: In announcing Operation Economic Outcast, the Trump administration said on Monday that it would involve choking off every last transaction that funnels money to Tehran.

item.title: U.S. Unveils Campaign to Cripple Iran’s Economy, but Offers Few Details
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent acknowledged the effort was more of a warning shot that would begin a period of “quiet diplomacy.”
item.dc:creator: Alan Rappeport
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the United States would “tighten the noose” around Iran by imposing sanctions on every source or facilitator of its revenue.

item.title: Iran Pledges to Defy Trump’s Economic Sanctions
item.description: Analysts say Tehran could intensify the dispute militarily after the United States announced new efforts to squeeze Iran’s economy. One Iranian official vowed that “not a single drop of oil” would leave the gulf.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Boxerman, Sanam Mahoozi and Ephrat Livni
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Motorists drive past an anti-American billboard in Tehran on Monday. President Trump has threatened Iran with “economic warfare and isolation on an unprecedented scale.”

item.title: Trump Lays It on the Line for Darline Graham Ahead of South Carolina Runoff
item.description: The president rallied for the sister of Lindsey Graham in her South Carolina Senate run and pressured allies to endorse her. A super PAC run by his advisers has spent nearly $800,000 on her campaign. Will it be enough?
item.dc:creator: Emily Davies, Patricia Mazzei and Michael Gold
item.media:description: President Trump rallied for Senator Darline Graham of South Carolina in Myrtle Beach, S.C., on Friday, part of a full-court press to secure her victory in a special runoff primary Tuesday to replace her late brother.

item.title: Jeffries Defends Kushner Meeting, Vowing Tough Oversight of Trump
item.description: The Brooklyn Democrat, who is in line to be speaker should his party win the House, has drawn ire from some progressives for huddling with the president’s son-in-law.
item.dc:creator: Annie Karni and Maggie Haberman

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed Joins Jesse Watters of Fox News for Some Light Verbal Combat
item.description: In a smiling yet tense interview, Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for Senate in Michigan, argued that his Republican critics were using culture-war issues to distract from Americans’ economic concerns.
item.dc:creator: Bayliss Wagner
item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times

item.title: California Judge Says Recalled Officials Are Unlawfully in Office
item.description: The mayor and three other council members of Avenal, Calif., had refused to leave despite a certified vote by residents to recall them. They will now step down, a city official said.
item.dc:creator: Livia Albeck-Ripka
item.media:credit: Philip Cheung for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Kings County Superior Court in Hanford, Calif.

item.title: Gov. Kathy Hochul, Five Years In, Makes Her Case for Four More
item.description: Ms. Hochul, who ascended to the governorship in the depths of the pandemic, believes that New York is back. She hopes she has persuaded New Yorkers.
item.dc:creator: Grace Ashford
item.media:credit: Amir Hamja for The New York Times
item.media:description: In five years of negotiating with state legislators, presidents and mayors, Gov. Kathy Hochul of New York has developed a distinctive political style.

item.title: The Mayor Went on Vacation. He Didn’t Travel Very Far.
item.description: Zohran Mamdani is known for working around the clock as mayor of New York City, but last week he and his wife headed “upstate” for vacation and some locals were thrilled to spot them.
item.dc:creator: Emma Goldberg
item.media:credit: Amir Hamja for The New York Times
item.media:description: Zohran Mamdani and Rama Duwaji, shown casting their votes for mayor last year, recently took a vacation in the Hudson Valley.

item.title: NYC’s 911 System Had an Outage. Officials Kept Quiet About It.
item.description: When a partial breakdown of the system occurred last week, New York City officials did not inform the public.
item.dc:creator: Chelsia Rose Marcius and Sally Goldenberg
item.media:credit: Dakota Santiago for The New York Times
item.media:description: A partial outage of the 911 system last week affected hundreds of callers in the Bronx.

item.title: S.E.C. Investigating Near-Implosion of A.I. Hedge Fund
item.description: Regulators sent subpoenas to major Wall Street banks seeking information about the trading of Situational Awareness, three people briefed on the outreach said.
item.dc:creator: Rob Copeland and Matthew Goldstein
item.media:credit: Nicholas Albrecht for The New York Times
item.media:description: Situational Awareness was founded two years ago by Leopold Aschenbrenner, formerly of OpenAI.

item.title: What You Should Know About College Admissions Changes
item.description: After loosening requirements during the Covid era, some schools are shaking up admissions again, facing pressure from the Trump administration, A.I. and even their own professors.
item.dc:creator: Alan Blinder and Mark Arsenault
item.media:credit: Kendrick Brinson for The New York Times
item.media:description: Can you use A.I. to apply to college? Will the school ask for your test scores? Some schools are changing their policies.

item.title: Religious References in Lindsay Clancy Trial Anger Judge and Defense
item.description: The religious reference by a prosecution witness on Monday incensed the presiding judge, who sternly instructed jurors to disregard it. Lindsay Clancy’s lawyer asked for a mistrial.
item.dc:creator: Maia Spoto and Jacey Fortin
item.media:description: Lindsay Clancy and her defense lawyer, Kevin Reddington, listen to testimony by Dr. Kirk Heilbrun, a forensic psychologist, on Monday.

item.title: Why the Lindsay Clancy Case Is Dividing Americans
item.description: She is being tried on murder charges for killing her three young children. The tragedy has resurrected debates over whether such women are criminals or victims.
item.dc:creator: Shaila Dewan
item.media:description: Lindsay Clancy in court during her murder trial on Wednesday in Plymouth, Mass.

item.title: Dale Dickey Is Way Past Crying in Barney Suits
item.description: Years ago, she donned a dinosaur costume to help make ends meet. Now she is a first-time Emmy nominee for her role in “Widow’s Bay.”
item.dc:creator: Dina Gachman and Maiwenn Raoult

item.dc:creator: Laura Chung
